dyn.ip_application.right_type.definition: The kind of intellectual property right the application is for (e.g. patent), as published by IP Australia. It scopes the application number, so the pair (right type, application number) identifies the application; it is not a statement about the party or the company.
dyn.ip_application.right_type.why_not_existing: The shortlist has no concept for IP right type; ext.licence.* concepts describe a licence held by a business, not an IP application's right type, and entity.entity_type describes the business subject, not the application.

dyn.party.address_post_code.definition: Postal code as supplied in the party's address on an IP application record, kept as raw text because formats are mixed and not normalised (e.g. '15666', '110044', '30024', 't6b 3n9'). It is a party address field only and is not a statement of the party's legal jurisdiction or of a business establishment location.
dyn.party.address_post_code.why_not_existing: address.postcode is owned by the business subject and implies a normalised business address; this value is an unnormalised party address field with non-Australian and alphanumeric formats, so owner, meaning and value domain differ.

dyn.party.abn.definition: Australian Business Number supplied for an IP application party, sparsely populated and unvalidated in this source. It is an identifier only and must not be used to infer legal form, company status or a link to a business entity.
dyn.party.abn.why_not_existing: entity.abn is owned by the business subject and is checksum-validated as a business identifier; here the value is an optional, sparse attribute of a party that may be an individual or an agent, so owner and validation scope differ.

dyn.party.address_country_code.definition: Country code as supplied in the party's address on an IP application record, lower-cased and unnormalised (e.g. 'us', 'hk', 'in', 'il'). It is a party address field only; it is not a statement of the party's legal jurisdiction, nationality or legal form.
dyn.party.address_country_code.why_not_existing: address.country is owned by the business subject and describes the business's own address country; this value is an unnormalised party address code on an IP application, so reuse would change owner and meaning.

dyn.party.address_state_code.definition: State or territory code as supplied in the party's address on an IP application record, lower-cased and unnormalised (e.g. 'vic', 'qld', 'nsw', 'wa'). It is a party address field only; it is not a statement of the party's legal jurisdiction, incorporation place or business operating location, and it must not be mapped onto the business subject's address.state enum without normalisation.
dyn.party.address_state_code.why_not_existing: address.state is an enum owned by the business subject with normalised Australian/NZ/OTHER values; this value is an unnormalised, lower-cased party address code owned by the IP-application party, so reuse would change both owner and value domain.

dyn.party.kind.definition: Whether the IP application party is recorded by the publisher as an organisation or an individual. This is a party classification only; it is not a legal form, not a company status, and never implies sole trader.
dyn.party.kind.why_not_existing: ext.entity.holder_kind is owned by the business subject and describes the holder of a business record; entity.entity_type is a business legal-structure guess. Neither is owned by an IP-application party, and reusing either would assert business legal form from a party classification.

dyn.party.identifier.definition: Publisher-assigned identifier for a party (organisation or individual) recorded on an IP application. It identifies the party across applications but is not a company registration number, ACN or ABN, and does not imply legal form or company status.
dyn.party.identifier.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept identifies an IP-application party; entity.acn and entity.abn are business registration identifiers owned by the business subject, and ext.licence.number identifies a licence, so reuse would change both owner and meaning.

dyn.party.role.definition: The publisher's specific role label for the party on the IP application (e.g. patentee, applicant, agent, opponent_agent). 'other' denotes a publisher role label outside the enumerated subset and is not a missing-value signal; 'unknown' is reserved for a blank source value. It is a distinct dimension from the role category and must not be collapsed with it; an agent role is not evidence of ownership of the right.
dyn.party.role.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept captures a party's specific role on an IP application; ext.licence.category describes a licence category held by a business, a different owner and meaning, so reuse would misstate the fact.

ext.entity.date_established.definition: Founding / establishment date. Not a registration date.

dyn.party.role_category.definition: The publisher's broad category of the capacity in which a party is recorded on an IP application (e.g. applicant, applicant_agent, opposition_agent, mortgagee). 'other' denotes a publisher category outside the enumerated subset (e.g. licensee) and is not a missing-value signal; 'unknown' is reserved for a blank source value. It is a role classification on the party-application involvement, not evidence of ownership of the right, not a legal form, and not a statement that the IP right is enforceable.
dyn.party.role_category.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept describes the capacity in which a party acts on an IP application; ext.contact.* and ext.licence.* concepts are owned by other entities and describe contact channels or licence authorisations, so reuse would change owner and meaning.

dyn.ip_application.number.definition: Publisher-assigned application number for an IP application, unique only within a given right type; it must be read together with the right type and is not a company registration number.
dyn.ip_application.number.why_not_existing: ext.licence.number identifies a licence held by a business, not an IP application; no shortlisted concept covers IP application identifiers, and the number is only meaningful scoped by right type.

ext.financial.total_income.definition: Total income as published for a stated reporting period. A fact for a period, not a current attribute.

ext.licence.end_date.definition: Publisher-stated end of the licence, not the end of the business or all its claims.

ext.licence.start_date.definition: Publisher-stated commencement of the licence, not the business establishment or registration date.

dyn.party.name.definition: Party name as published for an IP application party, lower-cased and unnormalised free text. It is a label only, not a unique identifier, and must not be used to join or deduplicate parties or to infer legal form.
dyn.party.name.why_not_existing: entity.legal_name and entity.trading_name are registered business names owned by the business subject; this value is an unnormalised party label on an IP application and may belong to an individual or an agent, so reuse would change owner and meaning.

entity.acn.definition: Australian Company Number. Also checksummed. The last 9 digits of an ABN are often the ACN, but not always.

ext.entity.holder_kind.definition: Whether the source says the record's holder is a natural person or an organisation. This is matching evidence. It never implies sole_trader.

ext.licence.status.definition: Licence status as published (licence status, not company status).

ext.entity.prior_registration_state.definition: State of original incorporation before national registration. Not an address.

ext.contact.role_email.definition: A role mailbox (info@, enquiries@, admin@ ...). Personal mailboxes are dropped by the transform.

ext.licence.authorisation_text.definition: Complete publisher authorisation text, including headings and conditions. Unparsed source evidence, not independent permission claims.

ext.entity.sector_tag.definition: A source-stated activity or beneficiary tag, e.g. scheme acnc_purpose or acnc_beneficiary. Keep the publisher's wording.

ext.entity.former_name.definition: A legal name the business held before its current one. Use valid_from/valid_to paths when the source dates the name. Never a trading name.

ext.entity.address_point.definition: lat,lon of the business's OWN stated address (e.g. a licensee's business address). A premises or site location is ext.establishment.geo on an establishment role instead.

entity_types.business: The source's business/legal-person subject; legal form remains unknown unless stated.
entity_types.licence: An authorisation held by a business.
entity_types.establishment: A physical operating facility, separate from its operator.
entity_types.ip_application: An IP application identified by the pair (ip_right_type, application_number); the right type scopes the application number.
entity_types.party: An organisation or individual recorded as a party on an IP application, identified by party_id; party_type distinguishes organisation from individual. Not a statement of legal form or company status.

PARTY_INVOLVED_IN_APPLICATION.definition: A party is recorded on an IP application in a specific party role (applicant, patentee, agent or other), for a party-activity validity period.

retrieval: Lexical shortlist only; reuse requires identical meaning, owner, units and scope. Missing candidates can be requested with a narrower task.
